title: Localization of graded sections at an invertible-module section
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme] (the intersection of any two affine opens is quasi-compact), $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent] $\mathcal O_X$-module. Put $X_s=\{x\in X:s(x)\ne0\text{ in }\mathcal L_x\otimes\kappa(x)\}$ and $N=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, where negative powers mean tensor powers of the dual invertible module. Multiplication by $s$ makes $N$ a graded module over $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$. The canonical map from the degree-zero part $N_{(s)}$ of its localization at $s$ to $\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal F)$, sending $t/s^n$ ($t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, $n\ge0$) to $t|_{X_s}\otimes(s|_{X_s})^{-n}$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), part (2), including equation module-invert-s

proof.text: For injectivity, suppose a homogeneous fraction $t/s^n$ maps to zero on $X_s$. The numerator $t$ is a global section of $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ whose restriction to $X_s$ is zero after division by the trivializing section $s^n$. Applying [lem-sc-p1-section-restriction-s-torsion] to this module and section gives $m\ge0$ for which multiplication by $s^m$ kills $t$. This is exactly the equivalence relation making $t/s^n$ zero in the localization.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), injectivity of the canonical map

proof.text: For surjectivity, let $u\in\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal F)$. Apply [lem-sc-p1-section-clearing-denominators-qcqs] to $X$, $\mathcal L$, $s$, $\mathcal F$, and $u$; its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses are those of the statement. It gives $m\ge0$ and $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes m})$ with $t|_{X_s}=u\otimes s^m$. The fraction $t/s^m$ therefore maps to $u$ under the canonical map.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PW (label lemma-invert-s-sections), surjectivity via clearing denominators
